subject: Operational headroom mapping & tranche bridging for renewal
messages:
From: Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@orbitalhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Munoz <alicia.munoz@orbitalhealth.com>, procurement@orbitalhealth.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal approaching — observed peak utilization and short-term GPU need

Hi Kimberly / Vanessa,

Renewal for our Dedicated pool is coming up in January and we pulled a utilization snapshot for November. We hit sustained 65–78% GPU utilization over multiple rolling windows when our nightly ensemble jobs run, and had two short bursts up to 92% (attached).

Before we sign the renewal amendment, procurement wants to understand options: can Redwood provision short-term headroom (bridging tranche) to cover spikes while we finalize the long-term commit? If so — what does that look like (size, expected lead time, billing)? Also curious whether there are software-level knobs you recommend to smooth those peaks in the meantime.

Happy to jump on a quick technical call this week.

Thanks,
Elliot
Ops Lead, Orbital Health

Attachments: util_snapshot_20261130.csv (CSV)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal approaching — observed peak utilization and short-term GPU need

Elliot — thanks for the snapshot. We looked through the CSV and agree the spikes are real and correlate with your nightly ensembles + some ad-hoc retrains. Two quick items:

1) Short-term bridging: we can spin up an 8-GPU tranche (A100-equivalent) on your Dedicated pool within 48–72 hours as a temporary headroom buffer. This would be billed as a monthly add-on with pro-rated first/last month.

2) Smoothing mitigations: Rishi has suggested workload-level batching improvements and KV-prefix caching for your ensemble workflow; those can reduce tail latency and lower peak active sequences. See Rishi's note below.

Proposed plan:
- Immediate: 8-GPU bridging tranche for 90 days (trial) — we monitor utilization daily.
- Review: if 30-day rolling average stays >=70% sustained, we recommend converting the tranche into a 24-GPU committed tranche and discuss an amortized discount for the remainder of the year.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call Thu or Fri to align on PO terms and an ops playbook? I'll attach our standard ops playbook and a one-page cost delta.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0147

Attachments: ops_playbook_v3.pdf (PDF)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 14:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal approaching — observed peak utilization and short-term GPU need

Adding technical detail from our infra side — copied Elliot for transparency. Key points: 

- Root cause: nightly ensembles (long-sequence evals) create KV cache churn and many long-lived KV contexts. This leads to inefficient batch fill rates at the start of windows and transient active-GPU spikes.
- Short-term mitigation (software):
  * Enable prefix/KV caching for the ensemble job (low-risk config change) — expected 8–12% reduction in token compute for those runs.
  * Apply workload-aware batching with a 100ms batching window for non-interactive jobs to improve utilization without impacting throughput.
- Hardware suggestion: add an 8-GPU bridging tranche now (A100-sim) to flatten tail spikes. Lead time 48–72 hours.
- Longer-term: if after 30 days the 30-day rolling average sustained utilization >=70%, convert to a 24-GPU committed tranche and provide a 12% monthly rate discount vs. on-demand tranche pricing (we'll put the exact numbers in the amendment).

Estimated cost delta (ballpark):
- 8-GPU bridging tranche: ~$28k/month (pro-rated first month)
- 24-GPU committed tranche (with discount): ~$72k/month (committed pricing)

I'll drop the ops playbook and a step-by-step runbook for enabling KV-prefix caching into the shared folder once we confirm the call.

—Rishi
Senior Infra PM, Redwood Inference

Cc: procurement@orbitalhealth.com, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 11:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal approaching — observed peak utilization and short-term GPU need

Thanks — appreciate the clear options. A couple procurement questions before we can approve the bridging tranche:

1) Billing cadence: Orbital prefers quarterly invoicing for addons if possible and a PO-led flow. Can Redwood support a quarterly invoice for the 8-GPU bridging tranche and pro-rate the first invoice to the tranche start date?
2) SLA/burst exception: because these spikes are operational-critical, can we add a 90-day SLA exception that preserves current latency SLOs while the bridge is active? We can include that in the amendment if Redwood is comfortable.
3) PO & terms: please send a one-page amendment + cost table so procurement can issue a PO quickly.

We can do the call Wed 12/8 at 10am ET.

Regards,
Alicia Munoz
Head of Ops, Orbital Health

Thanks all — appreciate the quick alignment on the call and the concrete asks. Summary and next steps below (we'll also drop a clean amendment doc and the PO-ready cost table to procurement):

Agreed trial plan:
- Provision an 8-GPU bridging tranche (A100-equivalent) on Orbital Health's Dedicated pool. Start: within 48–72 hours after PO. Duration: 90 days trial.
- Daily monitoring and a 30-day rolling utilization report. If 30-day rolling average >=70% at any review point, Redwood will propose conversion to a 24-GPU committed tranche with a 12% monthly rate discount for the committed period.
- Billing: Redwood can support quarterly invoicing for the tranche with pro-rated first invoice.
- SLA: Redwood will include a 90-day SLA exception to preserve current latency SLOs during the trial window (language to appear in amendment).

Action items: 
- Kimberly (me): share one-page amendment + cost table (DocSend link) and attach ops_playbook_v3.pdf. DONE.
- Karthik: prepare the draft addendum and cost table for signature (DocuSign).
- Rishi: share the KV-prefix caching runbook and enable a non-disruptive toggle on test for the ensemble job.
- Elliot / Alicia: procurement to send PO once amendment is received.

Timeline: aim to have PO and tranche provisioned by Wed, 12/15 if possible.

Thanks — I'll follow up with the DocuSign package and HubSpot update (DEAL-4827).

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0147
